stages.name: Foundations
stages.title: Company-level foundations
stages.note: Organisational requirements that must be in place before any product-specific work begins.

items.title: Documented Security Development Lifecycle
items.description: Maintain a documented SDL defining phases, roles and responsibilities. External certification (IEC 62443-4-1, ISO/IEC 27001) is optional but creates a presumption of conformity.

items.title: Evidence of conformity with the SDL
items.description: Where no external certification is held, keep documented evidence of internal conformity with the SDL.

items.title: SDL covers secure-by-design and secure-by-default
items.description: The SDL must explicitly address how the product minimises its attack surface without configuration by the end user.

items.title: EU Authorised Representative (non-EU manufacturers)
items.description: Manufacturers outside the EU must designate, by written mandate, a representative established in the EU, named in the technical documentation and the DoC.

stages.name: Before development
stages.title: Before development begins
stages.note: Classification, risk assessment and technical prerequisites set the scope for everything that follows.

items.title: Determine product classification
items.description: Identify whether the product is Default, Important Class I/II or Critical (Annexes III & IV). Classification determines the conformity assessment route.

items.title: Identify the conformity assessment route
items.description: Default: Module A self-assessment. Important Class I: Module A with a harmonised standard, else B+C or H. Important Class II & Critical: always via a Notified Body. Lead times of 4–10 months are common.

items.title: Product-specific cybersecurity risk assessment
items.description: Perform a risk assessment before development. Retain all versions; the initial pre-development version is part of the technical documentation.

items.title: Threat modelling
items.description: Identify attack surface, threat actors, attack vectors and resulting security requirements. Document the methodology used.

items.title: Third-party & open-source component policy
items.description: Define how third-party and open-source components are selected, evaluated and approved, including minimum EOL and vulnerability-response obligations.

items.title: EOL check for tools and dependencies
items.description: Check the End-of-Life date of all key tools, kernels, databases and libraries. Avoid components whose EOL falls within the product's support lifetime.

items.title: Storage encryption feasibility
items.description: Confirm the target hardware/runtime supports encryption of data at rest; a mandatory requirement that may force architectural adjustments.

items.title: Minimal attack-surface design
items.description: Plan to remove or disable by default every interface, service, port and protocol not required for the intended function.

items.title: Default credential policy
items.description: Ship with no default passwords, or force the user to set a unique credential on first use.

stages.name: During development
stages.title: During development
stages.note: Secure coding, testing and the update mechanism, evidenced throughout the build.

items.title: Cybersecurity-focused test plan
items.description: Test cases targeting authentication, access control, input validation, encryption and error handling. Documented and retained in the technical file.

items.title: Evidence of SDL compliance
items.description: Demonstrate, with documented evidence, that the SDL was followed at each phase.

items.title: Penetration testing / vulnerability assessment
items.description: Conduct security testing on the product or a representative build before release (DAST/SAST/Pen-test).

items.title: Secure software update mechanism
items.description: An authenticated, integrity-verified update mechanism, verifiable by the device before installation and automatic where feasible.

items.title: Data minimisation
items.description: Collect, process and store only the data strictly necessary for the intended function.

stages.name: Before release
stages.title: Before product release
stages.note: SBOM, network audit, EOL, conformity assessment, CE marking and the technical file.

items.title: SBOM prepared and vulnerability-screened
items.description: Prepare an SBOM covering at least all top-level dependencies and verify no component carries a known, already-patched vulnerability. Including a resolved CVE is a direct violation.

items.title: SBOM in machine-readable format
items.description: Store the SBOM as SPDX or CycloneDX (JSON/XML). PDF may be rejected as non-machine-readable.

items.title: Inbound connections list
items.description: List and individually justify every inbound connection and open port; remove or disable by default anything not required.

items.title: Outbound connections list
items.description: Audit and justify all outbound connections, including those from the OS, third-party libraries and telemetry.

items.title: Declare the product End-of-Life
items.description: Calculate and declare the EOL; it cannot exceed the EOL of key dependencies. Minimum 5-year support period unless the expected use lifetime is shorter.

items.title: Complete the conformity assessment
items.description: Carry out the applicable procedure (Module A, or B+C / H / Notified Body) and document it before affixing CE marking.

items.title: Prepare the EU Declaration of Conformity
items.description: Draft and sign the DoC per Annex V, referencing the regulation, product and assessment procedure. Keep available for 10 years.

items.title: Affix the CE marking
items.description: Apply visible, legible, indelible CE marking. No CE marking, no EU market from 11 Dec 2027.

items.title: Compile the technical file
items.description: Assemble the Annex VII package: description, risk assessment, SDL evidence, test results, SBOM, connection audits, DoC and EOL declaration.

items.title: 10-year retention plan
items.description: Archive all technical documentation, including every SBOM version, for at least 10 years from first market placement.

items.title: User-facing documentation
items.description: Communicate intended use, cybersecurity properties, how to configure security, the declared EOL and how to report vulnerabilities.

items.title: Vulnerability disclosure contact published
items.description: Publish a single, actively monitored point of contact for reporting vulnerabilities.

stages.name: After release
stages.title: After product release
stages.note: Ongoing monitoring, the Article 14 reporting timeline and update obligations across the support period.

items.title: Update risk assessment on significant change
items.description: Reassess when a major product change, significant new threat or exploited vulnerability is identified; document the trigger and outcome.

items.title: Automated SBOM vulnerability monitoring
items.description: Deploy tooling that monitors SBOM components against live feeds (NVD, EUVD, OSV) frequently enough to meet the 24-hour reporting window. Manual monitoring is insufficient.

items.title: 24-hour initial vulnerability report
items.description: On becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability, file an initial report within 24 hours via ENISA's single reporting platform. Applies from 11 Sep 2026.

items.title: 72-hour technical report
items.description: Submit a detailed technical report to ENISA and the national CSIRT within 72 hours, including severity and any mitigation.

items.title: Final report within 14 days of remediation
items.description: Submit a final report no later than 14 days after a security update or workaround is made available.

items.title: Severe incident reporting
items.description: Report severe incidents affecting product security on the same 24/72-hour timeline.

items.title: Automatic update for third-party vulnerabilities
items.description: Maintain an automatic update system able to patch third-party component vulnerabilities. A fix within 24 hours exempts reporting, not fixing.

items.title: Security updates free of charge
items.description: Provide all security updates free of charge for the duration of the support period.

items.title: Advance notice of End-of-Life
items.description: Notify users at least 12 months before the final security update, where feasible.

items.title: Corrective measures for non-compliant products
items.description: Remediate, withdraw or recall non-compliant products and notify market surveillance. Inaction is itself a violation.
